Masai Mara or Serengeti: which one to book

They are one ecosystem with a border through it. The right choice is about the month, the budget and how you like to travel.

The Masai Mara and the Serengeti are the same grassland, divided by the Kenya–Tanzania border. Wildebeest spend most of the year in Tanzania. They push into the Mara, usually from July into October, to use the northern grass. A crossing of the Mara River can happen on either side of that border.

Choose the Mara if this is your first safari, you have a week or less, and you are flying into Nairobi. The reserve is smaller, so game drives waste less time on transit. Camps sit close to the action in the migration months, which also means more vehicles at a sighting in August. A private vehicle still lets you leave a crowd and look elsewhere.

Choose the Serengeti if the migration itself is the subject and you can follow it. January and February on the southern plains, for the calving, is a Tanzania trip. There is no honest way to sell that month as a Mara migration safari. June in the western corridor is also Tanzania. July to October can be either, and many of the best weeks are in the far north of the Serengeti, looking at the same river from the other bank.

Tanzania park fees are higher. Kenya is usually the less expensive private safari for the same number of days, especially if you stay in mid-range lodges and drive rather than fly. Tanzania rewards an extra day and, often, a light aircraft seat.

You do not need both on a first trip of under ten days. The drive between them is not a scenic afternoon. If you have ten days and you want both, fly. If you have six, pick one country and see it properly.

A beach changes the sums. Zanzibar sits naturally on the end of a Tanzania safari. The Kenya coast, Diani or Watamu, sits naturally on the end of a Kenya safari. Either can be bolted onto the other with a flight, and we will show you that flight in the quote instead of hiding it.
